assumptions: Annual feed weights redistribute the inherited seed aggregate; they are an assumed gradual ramp, not a deployment solution. The separately recorded late feed is split equally between build years 7 and 8.

Coproduct refining starts in build year 3 and ramps to the selected final source share by year 8. Lunar treatment separately reaches 10% of total lunar feed, assumed to be selectable KREEP-like material. The lunar share is unchanged across source-refinery alternatives.

80% of refined product is allocated to Earth and 20% retained by the off-Earth economy, solely as an explicit allocation example; actual domestic demand and saleable export surpluses remain unestimated.

Source-to-Earth delay of 1.5 years is a planning proxy alongside the inherited three-year source round trip, not a derived trajectory; lunar delay of 0.25 years includes handling and dispatch. Sensitivities vary the source delay.
One-percent return loss is inherited from the capsule scenario and applied once. Refinery finishing recovery already covers processing losses.

Every material receipt is physical potential conditional on funded refining, delivery capacity, quality and buyers. The output does not assume bulk nickel, cobalt or a mixed rare-earth basket is automatically an economic Earth export.
